Repaint this blockout video as a finished hand-painted gouache animation. VERTICAL 9:16 portrait frame, frame for frame: keep the exact camera, framing, timing and every pose from the source video, and paint only what each source frame shows, adding no other characters or objects.

Character: the flame-shaped figure is Sol, exactly the mascot in the reference images (the turnaround sheet shows his shape from every side; the expression sheet shows every eye shape he makes). Round, plump gumdrop body with a red outer layer, an orange middle layer and a broad cream inner flame for the face. At rest his face is plain smooth cream with exactly two small tall navy #1C2447 oval eyes set low and close together, solid dark with no whites or highlights, and nothing else on it. His eyes change ONLY as the beats below say; copy his eyes from each source frame exactly, the same shape, size and place. Short stubby rounded red-orange arm nubs and two tiny blunt stubby red feet; his arm nubs stay the same short length in every frame and never stretch or grow. Sol wears nothing. Sol gives off no sparks, particles or smoke. His layers and face move together as one body with a small soft wobble that settles.

Scene: a kitchen counter seen from high above. A pale cream stone counter. On it lies one teal cloth with two white bowls of ice cubes side by side. Behind the bowls, in a row: one small white salt shaker with a rounded silver cap on the left, Sol in the middle, and one round yellow kitchen timer with a white dial on the right. The counter is painted stone with visible brushwork and soft cool shadows, not a flat blank colour. Warm morning sunlight with soft cool shadows, so the room has depth and glow. LETTERING RULE: every board, sheet of paper, card, tag and page in this shot is BLANK. Paint no letters, no numbers, no words, no symbols and no handwriting anywhere in the frame. Where the source video shows Sol's flame tip tinted deep indigo-violet, fading down into his normal orange, paint exactly that tint and exactly as much of it as each source frame shows. The few thin short navy vertical lines high on the left side of his face belong to that look: copy them only in the frames where the source shows them. 

Beats: 1. The salt shaker stands right against Sol's side. He looks to the left at it, leans over and bumps it with the side of his round body. PHYSICS RULE: the shaker slides a little to the left ONLY while his body is touching it, rocks once and stays upright where it stops; it is the same one-piece shaker in every frame. 2. At 2.2 seconds he turns and looks to the right at the kitchen timer, which stands right beside him, and does one small hop toward it, leaning its way. The timer never moves. ARM RULE: both arm nubs stay tucked at his sides for the whole shot; he never reaches, points or touches anything with an arm. 3. His flame tip keeps a faint indigo-violet tint at about half strength, with no thin lines. The bowls, the ice cubes and the cloth never change.

Style: match the painted reference frame from this same film exactly: the same paint treatment, the same palette, the same warm morning light and the same Sol. Where this shot is a different room, it is another room of the same house. Take every object's colour from the source video. Soft matte gouache painting with visible brushwork, broad simplified shapes, layered colour, softened painted edges and subtle paper texture on Sol, the props and the room alike. Forms defined by light and colour. No ink outlines, no black linework, not glossy 3D, not vector art. Smooth natural motion, no motion blur, stable background paint texture. No text, no captions, no speech, no music.
